name: Ixekizumab
route_note: Subcutaneous injection every 2 weeks initially, then every 4 weeks
tagline: Humanised IL-17A antibody for psoriasis and spondyloarthritis
summary: Ixekizumab is a humanised IgG4 monoclonal antibody that neutralises interleukin-17A. It is approved for plaque psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis and non-radiographic axial spondyloarthritis.
mechanism: Ixekizumab binds IL-17A (including the IL-17A/F heterodimer) with high affinity and blocks binding to the IL-17 receptor, reducing keratinocyte hyperproliferation and inflammatory signalling.
Its IgG4 backbone has minimal effector function; its effect results from cytokine neutralisation.
uses: Moderate to severe plaque psoriasis (adults and children ≥6 years)

history.title: Phase 2 results
history.detail: Phase 2 data in psoriasis are published in the New England Journal of Medicine.

history.title: FDA and EU approval
history.detail: Approved in March (US) and April (EU) for plaque psoriasis after the UNCOVER trials.

history.title: nr-axSpA and children
history.detail: Approved for non-radiographic axial spondyloarthritis and paediatric psoriasis.

pk.metabolism: Proteolytic catabolism to peptides and amino acids (no CYP metabolism)
pk.excretion: Not renally excreted as intact antibody; cleared by catabolism and target-mediated uptake

serious: New or worsening inflammatory bowel disease

facts: The SPIRIT-H2H trial compared ixekizumab head-to-head with adalimumab in psoriatic arthritis.
Injection-site reactions are among the most common adverse effects.
